name: @argszero/dsh-histexpand-guard
description: Refuses a bash command before it runs when the persistent shell would drop it to history expansion. The persistent bash tool writes each command into an interactive shell as one $'…' line, and an interactive bash expands history (`!…`) before parsing anything: an unresolvable designator makes it discard the whole line, the tool's end-of-command marker included, so the call hangs until its command deadline — 300 seconds by default — with no output and no reason. Reports of it arrive as timeout mysteries, because the commands look ordinary: `cat > x.sh <<'EOF'` with a `#!/usr/bin/env bash` body, `printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh'`, `git commit -m 'fix: wip!'`. The guard decides on the one fact that is certain from the text — whether history expansion reaches a `!` — using a rule calibrated against a real interactive bash (45/45 on the pinned corpus, scripts/calibrate-history-expansion.py) and refuses the call at tools/pre-execute, before the body runs and before any approval prompt. It refuses nothing else, never acts on the one-shot bash tool whose shell is not interactive, and fails open when its own scan errors. Zero runtime dependencies.
